ACCEPTThe exact identity  $D_F=2-S+A$ , the unique sparse-end ownership statement, and the initial covered-class inequality are correct under the stated hypotheses and granted dependencies. The potentially delicate step is the equality between the numbers of one- $P$  squares in the physical and shifted partitions. The note’s terminality argument justifies that equality, including for two-endpoint combs.The accounting uses each physical donor tile once and leaves every corrected endpoint-tile charge inside its whole receiver. The resulting criterion is genuinely a condition on the initial pair: the mouth labels, and hence  $S_H,A_H,D_H$ , are invariant during normalization.1. The square-connectivity assertion is justifiedThe statement needed in Section 2 is:For every unit square  $Q$ , the set  $P\cap Q$ , when nonempty, induces a connected subgraph.This holds for shifted squares as well as physical tiles.First, at a representative admitting no feasible single-edge promotion, every endpoint  $z\in P$  has occupied degree at least three. Otherwise, promoting  $z$  and deleting its actual mate would leave  $z$  with at most one occupied neighbor. Every previously selected vertex would retain or lose occupied neighbors, so all its feasibility constraints would remain satisfied. This would be a feasible single-edge promotion.Now suppose a unit square contains precisely two diagonal endpoints. Each of its other corners is adjacent to both endpoints and therefore cannot be selected. Since those corners are not endpoints either, they are blank. Each diagonal endpoint consequently has at most two occupied neighbors, both outside the square, contradicting the preceding degree bound.Two diagonal vertices are the only disconnected nonempty subset of the square’s four-cycle. Thus the assertion follows.Within a mouth, every endpoint belongs to a prescribed complete perpendicular straight comb. Connectedness therefore puts all endpoints of a square in one such comb. A square cannot contain endpoints in two columns: they would either connect distinct complete components or belong to a component that is not a straight single-column comb.There is also a direct check for the dangerous diagonal pattern in this particular contact class. A partial-column endpoint has its axial selected support in the other mouth row. If another comb supplied the diagonally opposite endpoint, that axial support would see both endpoints, violating feasibility. Thus the contact hypotheses themselves exclude the proposed diagonal escape.2. The three physical tile types are exactThe table in Section 2 is correct, including its assertions of exact selected counts.Full columnThe two consecutive comb endpoints have perpendicular supports on opposite sides. Exactly one support lies in the other column of the physical tile. That selected support already sees its intended endpoint and forces the remaining corner blank. Hence
$$(p,t)=(2,1),\qquad \mu=2.$$
This remains true if the comb starts at the upper mouth row or ends at the lower mouth row. It also includes a two-endpoint comb occupying exactly the two mouth rows.Saturated endIf the tile contains only one endpoint, the missing adjacent position in its column lies beyond the comb’s end. Its prescribed axial support therefore occupies that position inside the tile.When the endpoint’s perpendicular support also lies in the tile, there are exactly two selected vertices. The axial support forces the remaining corner blank:
$$(p,t)=(1,2),\qquad \mu=\frac52.$$
Sparse endWhen the perpendicular support points outside the tile, the axial support is the only selected vertex inside it.Both other corners are forced blank:The corner next to the axial support is forbidden by that support.The corner next to the endpoint is forbidden by the perpendicular support of the next endpoint along the comb. Alternation puts that support on the required side.The next endpoint exists even for a two-endpoint comb. Thus
$$(p,t)=(1,1),\qquad \mu=\frac32.$$
These blankness arguments prohibit additional endpoints as well as additional selected vertices. Required supports are actual vertices of the original rectangle, so the argument has no missing boundary-support case.3. The shifted partition has exactly  $E=S+U$  one- $P$  squaresThis is the essential partition bridge, and it is valid.Let  $C$  be the number of full endpoint columns in the mouth, and let  $E$  be the number of partial endpoint columns. The two boundary columns are blank.In either the physical or shifted partition:Every occupied column belongs to exactly one square.A full column contributes its two endpoints to that same square.A partial column contributes one endpoint.No square contains endpoints from two occupied columns, by the preceding square argument.Consequently, the number of physical one- $P$  tiles and the number of shifted one- $P$  squares are both exactly  $E$ . In particular,
$$E=S+U,\qquad |P\cap F|=2C+E.$$
There is no hidden assumption that physical and shifted tiles pair an endpoint with the same neighboring column. They generally do not. The proof only needs the number of partial columns to be preserved.4. The slack is nonnegative and integral, and the identity is exactThere are  $N-1$  shifted squares.A shifted square with no endpoint has at most two selected vertices. A square with a full endpoint column has at most one selected vertex. Each has raw weight at most two.A square with one endpoint has at most two selected vertices and therefore raw weight at most  $5/2$ . Since exactly  $E$  shifted squares have one endpoint,
$$\mu(F)\le 2(N-1)+\frac E2.$$
Thus
$$A:=2(N-1)+\frac E2-\mu(F)\ge0.$$
Using  $|P\cap F|=2C+E$  gives
$$\begin{aligned}
A
&=2(N-1)+\frac E2
  -|T\cap F|-\frac{2C+E}{2}\\
&=w-4-|T\cap F|-C.
\end{aligned}$$
Therefore  $A$  is an integer.The physical type table gives the exact decomposition
$$\mu(F)
=
2K+\frac{U-S}{2}
+\sum_{Q\in Z_F}t_Q.$$
Since  $Z_F$  contains  $N-K$  physical tiles,
$$\begin{aligned}
D_F
&=2(N-K)-\sum_{Q\in Z_F}t_Q\\
&=2N-\mu(F)+\frac{U-S}{2}.
\end{aligned}$$
Substitute
$$\mu(F)=2(N-1)+\frac{U+S}{2}-A$$
to obtain
$$\begin{aligned}
D_F
&=2-\frac{U+S}{2}+A+\frac{U-S}{2}\\
&=\boxed{2-S+A}.
\end{aligned}$$
All signs and half-unit terms cancel as claimed. In particular,
$$D_F\ge2-S.$$
As a consistency consequence,  $D_F\ge0$  also forces  $A\ge S-2$ . Thus the identity does not assign a negative deficit to a collection of no- $P$  tiles when several sparse ends occur.Relation to the original corrected ledgerOnly
$$D_F=\sum_{Q\in Z_F}(2-t_Q)$$
is assigned as payment. Every tile in that sum has no endpoint, so its original corrected charge is exactly  $t_Q-2$ .The raw weights of endpoint-containing tiles are used to derive this equality. Their corrected partial charges are never assigned to the mouth donor. Matching transfers across the mouth boundary therefore cause no defect.The slack  $A$  enters as part of the exact expression for the already identified donor  $D_F$ . It is not a second credit added on top of that donor.5. Sparse-end ownership is uniqueFor a complete vertical comb of even length, the physical paired column is on one fixed side of the comb throughout its length.There are two row phases.If the first endpoint occupies the first row of a physical row pair, the last endpoint occupies the second row of a pair. All endpoint tiles contain full two- $P$  columns.In the other phase, there are precisely two singleton endpoint tiles, one at each end. Both contain their axial support.In the second case, the perpendicular supports at the two endpoints point to opposite sides because the number of endpoints is even. Exactly one points into the paired physical column. Thus one end tile is saturated and the other is sparse.This includes a comb of length two. Rotation gives the horizontal case.Therefore every complete prescribed comb has at most one sparse physical end tile. Because the mouths are pairwise disjoint, that tile can occur in at most one  $S_H$ . The map
$$\{\text{sparse endpoint tiles lying in mouths}\}
\longrightarrow
\{\text{their complete comb owners}\}$$
is injective. Hence
$$\boxed{\sum_H S_H
\le
\#\{\text{distinct prescribed contact combs}\}.}$$
The more precise interpretation in the note is also correct: the left side counts exactly the distinct combs whose unique sparse physical end tile lies in a mouth. Other encounters with the same comb create no second sparse-end charge.6. The initial-to-final bridge is validAllowing a mouth to meet a comb end does not alter the comb’s freezing argument. Freezing depends on the even consecutive matching and the fixed axial and alternating perpendicular supports. Those data are unchanged.Thus every prescribed source and contact comb survives normalization with all its endpoints, matching edges, and supports. Since no endpoint is added, these preserved complete components remain complete and distinct.There is a useful stronger invariant here. Every initial endpoint in a mouth is frozen, and a promotion can add a selected vertex only at a promoted endpoint. Consequently:No endpoint in a mouth is deleted or promoted.No new selected vertex appears in a mouth.Original selected vertices remain.Original blank vertices remain blank.Therefore
$$T_{\mathrm{final}}\cap F_H=T_0\cap F_H,
\qquad
P_{\mathrm{final}}\cap F_H=P_0\cap F_H.$$
In particular,
$$S_H,\ U_H,\ C_H,\ K_H,\ A_H,\ D_H$$
are all determined by the initial configuration. The criterion  $S_{\mathrm{total}}\le B$  does not depend on an unknown choice of terminal normalization.For the remaining components, endpoint deletion preserves containment in two consecutive rows or columns and cannot create a new all- $P$  unit square. The granted nonpositive receiver theorem therefore applies to every nonprescribed final component.7. The disjointness dependencies apply, and the global ledger is exactThe new contact condition continues to exclude endpoints of one prescribed long source from another’s mouth. These are exactly the mutual exclusions required by the accepted separator argument. Its application is unaffected by the presence of comb ends.Thus the physical mouths are pairwise disjoint, and so are their no- $P$  subsets  $Z_{F_H}$ . At terminality, the granted tile-owner lemma puts those no- $P$  tiles outside every endpoint receiver.Before substituting the mouth identity, the global ledger can be written as
$$\begin{aligned}
\Delta
:={}&\frac{mn}{2}-|T_0|-|M_0|\\
={}&
\sum_{\mathrm{nonprescribed}\ J}-\rho(R_J)
-B+\sum_HD_H\\
&+\sum_{Q\in Z\setminus\bigcup_H Z_{F_H}}(2-t_Q).
\end{aligned}$$
Substitution of  $D_H=2-S_H+A_H$  gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\Delta
={}&
\sum_{\mathrm{nonprescribed}\ J}-\rho(R_J)
+B-S_{\mathrm{total}}+A_{\mathrm{total}}\\
&+\sum_{Q\in Z\setminus\bigcup_H Z_{F_H}}(2-t_Q),
\end{aligned}$$
which is exactly equation (4).Every term apart from  $B-S_{\mathrm{total}}$  is nonnegative:Nonprescribed whole receivers have nonpositive charge.Every  $A_H$  is nonnegative.Every remaining no- $P$  physical tile has at most two selected vertices.Hence
$$\boxed{|T_0|+|M_0|
\le\frac{mn}{2}-B+S_{\mathrm{total}}.}$$
Each whole comb receiver occurs once in the component sum. None of its endpoint tiles occurs in a donor set. A comb’s repeated encounters with mouths duplicate neither its whole receiver charge nor its sparse-end debt.The stated consequences follow:If  $S_{\mathrm{total}}\le B$ , then  $|T_0|+|M_0|\le mn/2$ .If  $S_{\mathrm{total}}<B$ , the deficit from  $mn/2$  is at least  $B-S_{\mathrm{total}}>0$ .If  $S_{\mathrm{total}}>B$ , coefficient one holds exactly when the three remaining nonnegative budgets in (4) total at least  $S_{\mathrm{total}}-B$ .The last statement is an exact reformulation of the ledger, without an automatic exterior-payment assertion.8. The coefficient-one sharpness claim has a written witnessThe previously supplied two-ending-comb configuration suffices by itself. Its mouth has three no- $P$  tiles with two selected vertices each and two sparse endpoint tiles. Hence
$$S=2,\qquad U=0,\qquad D_F=0.$$
It has  $w=12$ , eight selected mouth vertices, and no full endpoint column, so
$$A=w-4-|T\cap F|-C=8-8-0=0.$$
Any proposed uniform improvement
$$D_F\ge2-cS$$
would therefore require
$$0\ge2-2c,$$
forcing  $c\ge1$ .The one-end triple also has a direct realization from that same explicit configuration: remove the column- $7$  comb and its supports outside the mouth, while retaining its two selected mouth vertices. Removing those occupied vertices preserves feasibility. The remaining column- $4$  comb and long source retain their prescribed supports and remain frozen. The mouth then has
$$S=1,\qquad |T\cap F|=8,\qquad C=0,$$
so
$$A=0,\qquad D_F=1.$$
These explicit constructions establish sharpness independently of the reported optimization controls. The written proof establishes equations (2)–(5), with each sparse-end debt assigned to a distinct complete comb owner and every payment taken from an explicitly disjoint set of original no- $P$  tiles.
